collection.title: Noemorph philosophy-of-mind and global historical breadth additions
collection.method: Normalized exact-name and alias audit against the 249-record merged corpus, followed by record-level source checking against primary works, DOI-indexed scholarship, institutional editions, and specialist reference entries.
collection.source_policy: Every record retains at least two exact HTTPS locators and distinguishes original texts, translations, author-maintained copies, institutional editions, and authoritative secondary scholarship. No relationship edges or cross-tradition equivalences are asserted.
collection.coverage_note: This provisional shard broadens analytic philosophy, perception, self, agency, personal identity, phenomenology, ancient and early-modern psychology, and named Islamic, Jewish, Indian, East Asian, African, Maori, and Northern Ojibwe articulations. It is not exhaustive and does not treat any tradition as internally uniform.
exclusions: Homuncular functionalism was excluded as a version of the existing Functionalism record pending a version-level ontology.

Contingent representationalism and transparency theory were excluded because the current corpus already contains First-Order Representationalism and self-representational positions; a versioning policy is needed before splitting them.
Sensorimotor and enacted-perception candidates were excluded as duplicates of Sensorimotor Contingency Theory and Enactivism.
Radical neurophenomenology was excluded as a version of the existing Neurophenomenology record.

Named dual-aspect variants, Swinburne substance dualism, emergent dualism, neo-Thomist dualism, and Tye representationalism were excluded because the present ontology already contains their parent positions and does not yet support version records consistently.
Altered-state, anomalous-experience, and clinical challenge records were left to the separately scoped state-and-challenge audit.

records.name: Hard problem of consciousness
records.status_note: Chalmers's distinction remains influential, while physicalists dispute whether it marks a uniquely nonfunctional problem or an explanatory task that science can progressively constrain.
records.summary: Chalmers distinguishes explaining cognitive and behavioral functions from explaining why and how physical processing is accompanied by subjective experience. The hard problem is the latter explanatory demand, not the empirical search for neural correlates alone.
records.scope: Explanatory adequacy of physical and functional accounts of phenomenal experience.
records.boundary_note: The hard problem is not identical with Levine's explanatory gap or with the claim that consciousness is nonphysical; those require additional arguments.

claim_scope.applies_to: Accounts that explain functions without explaining why those functions are experienced.
claim_scope.does_not_establish: A particular nonphysical ontology or the impossibility of future explanation.

evidence_profile.citation_mix: Original formulation plus SEP overview.
evidence_profile.verification_summary: Author-hosted text and SEP locator checked.

open_questions: What would count as an explanation of phenomenal character rather than a correlation?
Can a revised physical or conceptual framework dissolve the apparent explanatory remainder?

citations.title: Facing Up to the Problem of Consciousness

records.name: Meta-problem of consciousness
records.tradition: Analytic philosophy of mind and cognitive science
records.status_note: The proposed research program is compatible with divergent views about phenomenal consciousness, although its explanatory significance is disputed.
records.summary: The meta-problem asks why humans make problem reports and judgments such as saying that experience is ineffable or hard to explain. Chalmers proposes explaining these report-generating cognitive processes independently of settling the hard problem itself.
records.scope: Mechanisms generating intuitions, judgments, and verbal reports about consciousness.
records.boundary_note: Explaining why people report a hard problem does not by itself explain phenomenal consciousness or show that phenomenal experience is illusory.

claim_scope.applies_to: Cognitive and social production of consciousness judgments.
claim_scope.does_not_establish: That the hard problem is solved, unreal, or reducible to report mechanisms.

evidence_profile.citation_mix: Author manuscript and university repository record for the same foundational work.
evidence_profile.verification_summary: Both exact locators checked; they document one primary publication rather than independent evidence.

open_questions: Which mechanisms generate specific anti-physicalist and ineffability intuitions?
How should explanations of reports constrain, without prejudging, theories of experience?

citations.title: The Meta-Problem of Consciousness
citations.venue: Australian National University Open Research Repository

records.name: Combination problem for panpsychism
records.status_note: Multiple variants concern subjects, qualities, structure, and intelligibility; proposed constitutive and nonconstitutive responses remain disputed.
records.summary: If fundamental entities possess experiential properties, a theory must explain how micro-level experiences or subjects yield a unified macro-level subject such as a human experiencer. The subject-combination form asks how many subjects could constitute one further subject.
proponents: David J. Chalmers as contemporary systematizer
records.scope: Constitutive explanation of macro-conscious subjects within panpsychist theories.
records.boundary_note: This is a family of objections, not one settled impossibility proof, and it applies differently to panpsychism, panprotopsychism, and cosmopsychism.

claim_scope.applies_to: The transition from putative microexperience to unified macroexperience.
claim_scope.does_not_establish: That every panpsychist or cosmopsychist model fails.

evidence_profile.citation_mix: Contemporary taxonomy plus SEP overview.
evidence_profile.verification_summary: OUP DOI and SEP locator checked.

open_questions: Can subjecthood be compositionally grounded at all?
Do nonconstitutive, emergent, or cosmopsychist accounts avoid or relocate the problem?

citations.venue: Panpsychism: Contemporary Perspectives, Oxford University Press

citations.title: Panpsychism
citations.authors: Philip Goff, William Seager, and Sean Allen-Hermanson

records.name: Causal exclusion problem for mental causation
records.tradition: Analytic metaphysics and philosophy of mind
records.status_note: Responses revise reduction, realization, causal inheritance, intervention, or exclusion premises; no consensus exists.
records.summary: If a physical event already has a sufficient physical cause, a distinct mental cause can appear redundant or to produce systematic overdetermination. Kim's exclusion reasoning presses nonreductive physicalists to explain how mental properties remain causally efficacious.
records.scope: Compatibility of mental causal efficacy with physical causal completeness.
records.boundary_note: The argument targets a conjunction of premises and does not independently prove epiphenomenalism or type identity.

claim_scope.applies_to: Accounts positing causally relevant mental properties alongside sufficient physical causes.
claim_scope.does_not_establish: That mental causation is impossible under every ontology.

evidence_profile.citation_mix: Kim's exclusion formulation plus SEP survey.
evidence_profile.verification_summary: Cambridge DOI and SEP locator checked.

open_questions: Must causes compete at the same explanatory level?
Can realization or interventionist accounts secure mental efficacy without overdetermination?

citations.title: Mechanism, Purpose, and Explanatory Exclusion
citations.venue: Supervenience and Mind, Cambridge University Press

citations.title: Mental Causation
citations.authors: David Robb, John Heil, and Sophie Gibb

records.name: Inverted spectrum argument
records.status_note: Debate concerns conceivability, behavioral and functional indistinguishability, relational color structure, and whether the case is metaphysically possible.
records.summary: Two people might be functionally and behaviorally alike while systematically differing in color experience—for example, the experience one has for red matching the other's experience for green. If coherent, the case challenges views that individuate phenomenal character wholly by functional role.
records.scope: Whether phenomenal character is fixed by functional, behavioral, or representational organization.
records.boundary_note: The argument concerns a stipulated systematic inversion, not ordinary individual differences in color discrimination.

claim_scope.applies_to: The claim that functional organization exhaustively fixes qualitative character.
claim_scope.does_not_establish: That actual undetectable inversions occur or that qualia are nonphysical.

evidence_profile.citation_mix: Shoemaker's modern treatment plus SEP.
evidence_profile.verification_summary: JSTOR DOI and SEP locator checked.

open_questions: Can a total inversion preserve every discriminatory and affective relation?
Does phenomenal character have an intrinsic component beyond representational structure?

records.name: Argument from hallucination
records.status_note: Disjunctivists reject a shared experiential kind, while sense-data, representational, and relational theories analyze the inference differently.
records.summary: A subject can hallucinate an experience introspectively indiscriminable from veridical perception. A common-kind inference holds that both experiences therefore share an immediate experiential nature, creating pressure on direct relational accounts of perception.
proponents: A. J. Ayer and other common-kind theorists
M. G. F. Martin as a critical analyst
records.scope: What veridical perception and subjectively indistinguishable hallucination have in common.
records.boundary_note: The label covers several arguments; indiscriminability alone does not transparently entail sameness of fundamental experiential kind.

claim_scope.applies_to: The metaphysical structure of veridical and hallucinatory experience.
claim_scope.does_not_establish: A single preferred theory of perception without further premises.

evidence_profile.citation_mix: Disjunctivist analysis plus SEP taxonomy.
evidence_profile.verification_summary: Springer DOI and SEP locator checked.

open_questions: What notion of indiscriminability is relevant?
Can hallucinations be characterized without positing a common perceptual object or state kind?

records.name: Problem of other minds
records.status_note: Analogical, criterial, inferential, perceptual, enactive, and social-practice responses disagree about whether the problem's skeptical framing is compulsory.
records.summary: One has first-person access to one's own mental life but encounters others through bodies, actions, and speech. The problem asks what warrants belief that others have minds and whether mental states can be perceived or only inferred.
proponents: John Stuart Mill as analogical theorist
records.scope: Epistemic grounds for attributing mentality and experience to others.
records.boundary_note: The philosophical problem is not identical to empirical theory-of-mind tasks, although findings about social perception may bear on proposed solutions.

claim_scope.applies_to: Justification and conceptual grounds for other-mind attribution.
claim_scope.does_not_establish: That other minds are unknowable or that one inferential model is mandatory.

evidence_profile.citation_mix: Classic criterial treatment plus SEP survey.
evidence_profile.verification_summary: JSTOR DOI and SEP locator checked.

open_questions: Can another's emotions or intentions be directly perceived?
How much justification rests on shared practices rather than analogy?

records.name: Molyneux's problem
records.tradition: Early modern and contemporary philosophy of perception
records.status_note: Modern surgery studies constrain some readings, but the original question leaves training, touch, vision, and concept possession underspecified.
records.summary: Molyneux asked whether a person born blind who learned to distinguish a cube and sphere by touch could, upon gaining sight, identify them visually without touching them. The case probes whether spatial concepts or object representations transfer innately across modalities.
records.scope: Cross-modal object recognition and the experiential basis of spatial representation.
records.boundary_note: The historical question cannot be mapped directly onto a single modern experiment without specifying visual competence, delay, learning, and task demands.

claim_scope.applies_to: Relations among tactile and visual object representations.
claim_scope.does_not_establish: A simple victory for nativism or empiricism.

evidence_profile.citation_mix: Locke's Essay plus SEP historical and empirical review.
evidence_profile.verification_summary: Project Gutenberg edition and SEP locator checked.

open_questions: Which spatial invariants are shared across modalities before learning?
How do rapid post-surgical learning and deprivation effects bear on the original case?

citations.title: An Essay Concerning Human Understanding, Book II, Chapter IX
Molyneux's Problem
citations.authors: Brian Glenney, Gabriele Ferretti, and Marjolein Degenaar

records.name: Fission and branching problem for personal identity
records.status_note: Responses deny branching identity, privilege one continuer, revise identity, or argue that psychological continuity matters without numerical identity.
records.summary: If one person's psychology is equally continued in two future people, a one-to-one identity relation cannot straightforwardly connect the original to both. Parfit uses fission to separate what matters in survival from strict numerical identity.
records.scope: Whether psychological continuity can ground identity under branching.
records.boundary_note: Fission is a family of stipulated cases and should not be presented as a demonstrated future technology or ordinary dissociative condition.

claim_scope.applies_to: One-to-many psychological continuity and the logic of persistence.
claim_scope.does_not_establish: That persons do not exist or that identity never matters practically.

evidence_profile.citation_mix: Parfit's canonical treatment plus SEP taxonomy.
evidence_profile.verification_summary: OUP DOI and SEP locator checked.

open_questions: Can persistence be non-branching by definition without becoming arbitrary?
What grounds prudential concern if identity is not what matters?

records.name: Subjective-character challenge from 'What Is It Like to Be a Bat?'
records.status_note: Nagel frames limits on current objective conceptions; whether the argument supports nonphysicalism, perspectival facts, or methodological reform remains disputed.
records.summary: Nagel argues that a conscious organism has a subjective character—there is something it is like for that organism. An objective physical description may omit the organism's point of view even when it captures structure and function.
records.scope: Whether objective descriptions can capture the perspectival character of experience.
records.boundary_note: Nagel's argument does not simply infer that bat experience is unknowable or that mind is a separate substance; it diagnoses a mismatch between available concepts and subjective facts.

claim_scope.applies_to: Objective accounts that omit what experience is like for its subject.
claim_scope.does_not_establish: Substance dualism or absolute incommunicability of experience.

evidence_profile.citation_mix: Original article plus SEP orientation.
evidence_profile.verification_summary: JSTOR DOI and SEP locator checked.

open_questions: Can objective concepts be transformed to include perspectival structure?
How much of another species' experience can empirical modeling recover?

citations.title: What Is It Like to Be a Bat?

records.name: Phenomenal concept strategy
aliases: phenomenal concept account of the explanatory gap
records.status: major physicalist response family · actively contested
records.status_note: Different accounts treat phenomenal concepts as recognitional, quotational, indexical, or otherwise cognitively distinctive; critics dispute whether conceptual difference explains the modal and epistemic intuitions.
records.summary: Phenomenal concept strategies argue that the apparent gap between physical knowledge and first-person phenomenal knowledge arises from distinctive ways of thinking about experiences rather than from nonphysical properties. The same physical state may be represented by very different physical and phenomenal concepts.
records.scope: Physicalist explanations of knowledge, conceivability, and explanatory-gap intuitions.
records.boundary_note: This is a response family, not one uniform theory; success requires more than noting that two concepts differ.

claim_scope.applies_to: Why phenomenal and physical judgments can seem independent even if their referents are physical.
claim_scope.does_not_establish: Physicalism without a defensible account of the relevant concepts and their epistemic behavior.

evidence_profile.citation_mix: Papineau's developed account plus SEP physicalism survey.
evidence_profile.verification_summary: OUP DOI and SEP locator checked.

open_questions: Which account of phenomenal concepts explains their alleged cognitive isolation?
Can the strategy answer both knowledge and conceivability arguments without circularity?

records.name: Animalism about personal identity
records.status_note: Animalists disagree about biological persistence conditions; psychological and constitution theorists dispute that persons are fundamentally organisms.
records.summary: Animalism holds that each human person is numerically identical with a human animal. Persistence therefore follows the continued life or biological organization of the organism rather than requiring continuity of memory, personality, or consciousness.
records.scope: What human persons are and what grounds their persistence.
records.boundary_note: Animalism does not imply that psychological properties are unimportant; it denies that they constitute numerical persistence of the human animal.

claim_scope.applies_to: The numerical identity and persistence of human persons.
claim_scope.does_not_establish: A complete theory of personhood, moral status, or consciousness.

evidence_profile.citation_mix: Olson's monograph plus SEP taxonomy.
evidence_profile.verification_summary: OUP DOI and SEP locator checked.

open_questions: Which biological event begins or ends the animal's existence?
How should animalism handle cerebrum-transplant and multiple-occupancy cases?

citations.title: The Human Animal: Personal Identity Without Psychology

records.name: Psychological-continuity theory of personal identity
records.status: major position family · branching and circularity contested
records.status_note: Contemporary views replace direct memory with overlapping chains of psychological connectedness, but disagreement persists about circularity, duplication, and embodiment.
records.summary: A person persists insofar as later mental life stands in the right causal continuity with earlier mental life through memory, intention, character, and other psychological connections. Neo-Lockean versions distinguish genuine continuity from merely copied information.
records.scope: Psychological conditions for diachronic personal persistence.
records.boundary_note: The contemporary family is broader than Locke's consciousness criterion and must specify a noncircular causal account of apparent memory.

claim_scope.applies_to: Identity or survival across changes in body and psychology.
claim_scope.does_not_establish: That bodily continuity never matters or that branching can preserve one-to-one identity.

evidence_profile.citation_mix: Parfit's influential revision plus SEP overview.
evidence_profile.verification_summary: OUP DOI and SEP locator checked.

open_questions: What causal relation makes an apparent memory identity-preserving?
Should branching preserve survival without preserving identity?

records.name: Narrative self-constitution view
records.status_note: Narrative theorists disagree about whether narrative constitutes identity, practical personhood, agency, or intelligibility; critics challenge narrative requirements and exclusion risks.
records.summary: Schechtman's narrative self-constitution view holds that persons constitute identities by organizing experiences and projects into an intelligible life narrative constrained by reality and by interpersonal articulation. The view concerns practical identity and personhood more than bare organism persistence.
records.scope: How temporally extended self-interpretation structures practical identity.
records.boundary_note: Narrative views are not equivalent to the psychological-continuity criterion and should not imply that every person must tell a polished verbal autobiography.

claim_scope.applies_to: Unity, agency, and self-understanding across a life.
claim_scope.does_not_establish: A necessary condition for biological persistence or consciousness.

evidence_profile.citation_mix: Foundational monograph plus SEP ethical identity survey.
evidence_profile.verification_summary: Cornell DOI and SEP locator checked.

open_questions: How demanding can narrative coherence be without excluding atypical cognition?
What distinguishes constitutive narrative from retrospective interpretation?

records.name: Constitution view of persons
records.status: major alternative to animalism · actively contested
records.status_note: Critics press coincidence and counting objections; defenders distinguish constitution from identity and appeal to first-person capacities.
records.summary: Baker's constitution view holds that a person is constituted by a human body without being numerically identical to that body, as a statue is constituted by but not identical to its matter. A first-person perspective is central to the kind person.
records.scope: Relation between persons and organisms and the persistence of each.
records.boundary_note: Constitution is presented as a nonidentity relation, not a claim that a person floats free of an organism.

claim_scope.applies_to: How a person depends on and is constituted by a body.
claim_scope.does_not_establish: Substance dualism or independence from biological realization.

evidence_profile.citation_mix: Baker's book plus SEP personal-identity survey.
evidence_profile.verification_summary: Cambridge DOI and SEP locator checked.

open_questions: How many coincident entities occupy the same place?
Can first-person capacities ground a distinct substance kind without circularity?

citations.title: Persons and Bodies: A Constitution View

records.name: Semantic externalism about mental content
records.tradition: Analytic philosophy of mind and language
records.status_note: Natural-kind, social, and anti-individualist versions differ; debates concern self-knowledge, causal explanation, and narrow content.
records.summary: Semantic externalism holds that at least some mental contents are partly individuated by relations to the physical or social environment rather than solely by intrinsic properties of the thinker. Putnam's Twin Earth case makes chemically different environments yield different water-thought contents despite internal similarity.
records.scope: Individuation of intentional mental content by environmental and social relations.
records.boundary_note: Externalism about content does not by itself make vehicles of thought spatially external or imply the extended-mind thesis.

claim_scope.applies_to: What determines the referential content of some thoughts.
claim_scope.does_not_establish: That all cognition is extended or that internal organization is explanatorily irrelevant.

evidence_profile.citation_mix: Putnam's canonical formulation plus SEP survey.
evidence_profile.verification_summary: Cambridge DOI and SEP locator checked.

open_questions: Can externalist content play the causal roles required by psychology?
How is privileged self-knowledge compatible with environmentally individuated content?

citations.title: The Meaning of 'Meaning'
citations.venue: Mind, Language and Reality, Cambridge University Press

citations.title: Externalism About the Mind
citations.authors: Mark Rowlands, Joe Lau, and Max Deutsch

records.name: Teleosemantics
records.status_note: Consumer, producer, informational, and selected-effects variants differ; Swampman, indeterminacy, and novel-content objections remain live.
records.summary: Teleosemantic theories explain representational content through biological functions shaped by selection or functionally reproduced systems. A representation's correctness conditions are tied to what its producing or consuming mechanisms are for, allowing misrepresentation to be analyzed normatively without irreducible semantics.
records.scope: Naturalistic grounding of mental content, correctness, and misrepresentation.
records.boundary_note: Teleosemantics is a family of content theories, not a theory of phenomenal consciousness, and not every appeal to function is evolutionary selected-effects semantics.

claim_scope.applies_to: How representational states acquire correctness conditions.
claim_scope.does_not_establish: That phenomenal character reduces to biological function.

evidence_profile.citation_mix: Millikan's foundational system plus SEP taxonomy.
evidence_profile.verification_summary: MIT Press DOI and SEP locator checked.

open_questions: Can selected functions determine sufficiently specific content?
How does the account handle novel, abstract, or culturally acquired representations?

citations.title: Language, Thought, and Other Biological Categories

records.name: Causal theory of action
records.status: standard account family · deviant causation contested
records.status_note: Causalists differ over intentions, reasons, and guidance; noncausalists argue that agency cannot be reduced to event-causal chains.
records.summary: On Davidson's influential view, an action is an event caused in the appropriate way by an agent's reasons—typically beliefs and pro-attitudes that rationalize it. The view explains action as a species of causally produced behavior while preserving reason explanation.
records.scope: Difference between intentional action and mere bodily happening.
records.boundary_note: Causation must occur in a nondeviant, guidance-relevant way; mere causal contribution by a desire and belief is insufficient.

claim_scope.applies_to: How reasons and intentions produce and explain actions.
claim_scope.does_not_establish: Free will, moral responsibility, or agent causation.

evidence_profile.citation_mix: Davidson's canonical paper plus SEP action survey.
evidence_profile.verification_summary: JSTOR DOI and SEP locator checked.

open_questions: What distinguishes nondeviant from deviant causal chains?
Are reasons causes, constitutive explanations, or both?

citations.title: Action
citations.authors: Juan S. Piñeros Glasscock and Sergio Tenenbaum

records.name: Agent-causal theory of action
records.status_note: Defenders treat agents as irreducible causes of choices; critics dispute intelligibility, empirical fit, and whether agent causation improves control over event-causal indeterminism.
records.summary: Agent-causal theories hold that in some free actions the agent, construed as a persisting substance, directly causes an intention or action without that causal contribution reducing to causation by prior events. Reasons may influence without determining the choice.
records.scope: Irreducible agential control in intentional action and libertarian freedom.
records.boundary_note: Agent causation is not simply any action caused by a person; it posits a distinctive causal relation not reducible to event causation.

claim_scope.applies_to: Sourcehood and control in putatively free choices.
claim_scope.does_not_establish: That humans actually instantiate agent causation or that indeterminism alone yields responsibility.

evidence_profile.citation_mix: O'Connor's author-hosted chapter plus SEP survey.
evidence_profile.verification_summary: Author manuscript and SEP locator checked.

open_questions: How can agent causation be integrated with causal explanation in science?
What settles a choice if prior reasons do not determine it?

citations.title: Incompatibilist (Nondeterministic) Theories of Free Will
citations.authors: Randolph Clarke, Justin Capes, and Philip Swenson

records.name: Frankfurt's hierarchical account of free will
records.status: foundational compatibilist account · regress and manipulation contested
records.status_note: Later identification theories revise the hierarchy to address regress, ambivalence, and social formation of higher-order desires.
records.summary: Frankfurt distinguishes first-order desires from second-order desires about which desires should move one to action. A person exercises freedom of the will when the effective first-order desire accords with a second-order volition with which the person identifies.
records.scope: Reflective identification, personhood, and compatibilist freedom.
records.boundary_note: The account concerns structure of willing, not phenomenal levels of consciousness, and higher-order endorsement may itself be manipulated or conflicted.

claim_scope.applies_to: When an agent's effective desire expresses the will the agent wants.
claim_scope.does_not_establish: Ultimate sourcehood or exemption from causal determination.

evidence_profile.citation_mix: Frankfurt's foundational paper plus SEP free-will survey.
evidence_profile.verification_summary: JSTOR DOI and SEP locator checked.

open_questions: What stops a regress of higher-order endorsements?
Can socially shaped or manipulated volitions ground authentic identification?

citations.title: Freedom of the Will and the Concept of a Person

records.name: Sense-data theory of perception
records.status_note: The view shaped twentieth-century debates but faces the veil-of-perception, ontological, and phenomenal-location objections; contemporary versions are more limited.
records.summary: Sense-data theories hold that in perception a subject is directly aware of mind-dependent or nonordinary objects that bear the apparent qualities of the perceived scene. Physical objects are known indirectly through these immediate data.
proponents: G. E. Moore in some periods
records.scope: Immediate objects of awareness in perception and hallucination.
records.boundary_note: Sense-data are theoretical immediate objects, not raw receptor measurements or the ordinary sensory data recorded in experiments.

claim_scope.applies_to: What is directly present in veridical and nonveridical experience.
claim_scope.does_not_establish: Skepticism about external objects or a neural theory of perception.

evidence_profile.citation_mix: Russell's public-domain exposition plus SEP taxonomy.
evidence_profile.verification_summary: Project Gutenberg and SEP locators checked.

open_questions: What kind of entity is a sense-datum?
Can the view explain awareness of external objects without an unacceptable perceptual veil?

records.name: Disjunctivism about perception
records.status: major contemporary position family · actively contested
records.status_note: Metaphysical, epistemological, and phenomenal disjunctivisms must be distinguished; critics challenge negative characterizations of hallucination.
records.summary: Perceptual disjunctivism denies that a veridical perception and an introspectively indiscriminable hallucination must share the same most fundamental mental kind. In the good case, experience can constitutively relate the subject to an external object.
records.scope: Fundamental nature and epistemic standing of veridical and hallucinatory experiences.
records.boundary_note: Disjunctivism is related to but not identical with naïve realism; some disjunctivist claims concern knowledge rather than experiential metaphysics.

claim_scope.applies_to: Whether good and bad perceptual cases share a fundamental experiential kind.
claim_scope.does_not_establish: That hallucinations lack phenomenal character or that every disjunctivist is a naïve realist.

evidence_profile.citation_mix: Martin's influential account plus SEP taxonomy.
evidence_profile.verification_summary: Springer DOI and SEP locator checked.

open_questions: Can hallucination be positively characterized without reintroducing a common factor?
How does disjunctivism accommodate neural and phenomenal similarities?

records.name: Gibsonian ecological approach to perception
records.status: major perception framework · active empirical program
records.status_note: Ecological psychologists dispute representationalist assumptions, while debates continue over information richness, affordance ontology, and neural implementation.
records.summary: Gibson's ecological approach treats perception as direct pickup of information available in structured ambient arrays by an active organism. Perceivers detect affordances—environmental possibilities for action relative to their capacities—without first reconstructing an impoverished retinal input into an inner picture.
records.scope: Organism-environment information, active exploration, and perception of affordances.
records.boundary_note: Direct perception does not mean receptor-free or inference-free in every sense; it rejects a particular mediational reconstruction picture and remains distinct from naïve realism as a metaphysical thesis.

claim_scope.applies_to: Information available to active organisms in ecological settings.
claim_scope.does_not_establish: That neural processing is absent or that every perceptual judgment is veridical.

evidence_profile.citation_mix: Gibson's foundational book plus SEP contextualization.
evidence_profile.verification_summary: Routledge DOI and SEP locator checked.

open_questions: How should affordances be individuated across organisms and social practices?
What neural dynamics realize direct pickup without reverting to reconstruction?

citations.title: The Ecological Approach to Visual Perception

records.name: Embodied cognition thesis
records.tradition: Cognitive science and philosophy of mind
records.status: large research family · strong and weak theses contested
records.status_note: Claims range from bodily constraint and sensorimotor dependence to constitutive embodiment; treating them as one thesis overstates consensus.
records.summary: Embodied approaches hold that cognitive capacities are deeply shaped, enabled, or partly constituted by bodily form, sensorimotor activity, affect, and environmental coupling. Varela, Thompson, and Rosch combined cognitive science with phenomenology to challenge a disembodied symbol-processing picture.
records.scope: Roles of bodily morphology and sensorimotor engagement in cognition.
records.boundary_note: Embodied cognition is broader than enactivism, extended mind, or the sensorimotor theory of perception; each makes different constitutive commitments.

claim_scope.applies_to: How bodily organization contributes to cognitive processes.
claim_scope.does_not_establish: That all cognition is nonrepresentational or spatially extended.

evidence_profile.citation_mix: Primary programmatic book plus SEP taxonomy.
evidence_profile.verification_summary: MIT Press DOI and SEP locator checked.

open_questions: Which cognitive processes are merely causally dependent on bodies and which are constituted by them?
How can embodied accounts generate precise comparative predictions?

citations.title: The Embodied Mind: Cognitive Science and Human Experience
citations.authors: Francisco J. Varela, Evan Thompson, and Eleanor Rosch

records.name: Bicameral-mind hypothesis
records.status: historically influential hypothesis · highly speculative and non-consensus
records.status_note: Its neurological lateralization and philological chronology have not been established; modern scholarship treats it as provocative but weakly evidenced.
records.summary: Jaynes proposed that some ancient humans lacked modern introspective, narratized consciousness and experienced internally generated commands as external divine voices, with a cultural transition producing the later conscious mind. He linked the proposal to language, texts, social organization, and hemispheric specialization.
records.scope: A proposed historical transition in human introspective cognition and command hallucination.
records.boundary_note: The hypothesis is not the generic claim that brains have two hemispheres, and its special definition of consciousness differs from many contemporary phenomenal and access-consciousness constructs.

claim_scope.applies_to: Jaynes's proposed culturally mediated transition in introspective mentality.
claim_scope.does_not_establish: That ancient people lacked all awareness, that schizophrenia is an evolutionary relic, or that lateralization evidence validates the chronology.

evidence_profile.citation_mix: Author-society full-text locator plus PubMed-indexed appraisal.
evidence_profile.verification_summary: Primary locator and PubMed metadata checked.

open_questions: Can the textual chronology be tested independently of interpretive assumptions?
Which claims, if any, survive current evidence about inner speech and auditory hallucination?

citations.title: The Origin of Consciousness in the Breakdown of the Bicameral Mind
The 'Bicameral Mind' 30 Years On: A Critical Reappraisal of Julian Jaynes' Hypothesis
citations.authors: Andrea Eugenio Cavanna, Michael Trimble, Federico Cinti, and Francesco Monaco

records.name: Velmans's reflexive monism
records.status_note: The view is discussed in consciousness studies but is not a consensus scientific theory; questions remain about causal explanation and its relation to dual-aspect monism.
records.summary: Velmans argues that the experienced world is a perspectival representation constructed through brain processes yet phenomenally located where objects appear, not inside the brain. Reflexive monism treats observers and experienced worlds as differentiated aspects of one encompassing universe.
records.scope: Relations among brain processing, phenomenal space, external world, and observer perspective.
records.boundary_note: This named view is not interchangeable with the existing generic Dual-aspect monism record; its distinctive claim concerns reflexive embedding and phenomenal location.

claim_scope.applies_to: How phenomenal worlds relate to brains, external causes, and observer perspectives.
claim_scope.does_not_establish: A validated neural mechanism or literal emission of experience from the brain.

evidence_profile.citation_mix: Peer-reviewed handbook statement plus university-maintained publication record.
evidence_profile.verification_summary: Wiley DOI and Goldsmiths locator checked.

open_questions: What explanatory work is performed by reflexivity beyond dual-aspect description?
How can the view be distinguished empirically from representational alternatives?

records.name: Stoljar's epistemic view of the consciousness problem
records.status_note: The proposal explains anti-physicalist intuitions through ignorance of relevant physical truths; critics dispute whether the hypothesized ignorance is independently motivated.
records.summary: Stoljar proposes that the apparent conflict between consciousness and physicalism may arise because human thinkers are ignorant of a class of physical facts relevant to experience. Conceivability judgments formed under that ignorance need not reveal a metaphysical gap.
records.scope: Epistemic origin of conceivability and explanatory problems for consciousness.
records.boundary_note: The view is not generic nonreductive physicalism and does not specify the unknown physical facts; it is a named diagnosis of why anti-physicalist reasoning may mislead.

claim_scope.applies_to: How ignorance can generate apparent gaps between physical and phenomenal descriptions.
claim_scope.does_not_establish: Which unknown physical facts exist or a completed reduction of consciousness.

basis: authoritative reference entry by the same philosopher
evidence_profile.citation_mix: OUP book plus SEP physicalism taxonomy.
evidence_profile.verification_summary: OUP DOI and SEP locator checked.

open_questions: What independently supports the postulated category of unknown physical facts?
Can the view explain stable phenomenal concepts without merely restating ignorance?

records.name: Platonic tripartite soul
records.status_note: Scholars debate whether the parts are agents, motivational sources, or structural roles and how the Republic relates to Plato's other dialogues.
records.summary: In the Republic, Plato distinguishes rational, spirited, and appetitive sources of motivation to explain psychic conflict and justice. A well-ordered soul is governed by reason with spirit appropriately allied to it, while appetite is regulated rather than erased.
records.scope: Psychic conflict, motivation, virtue, and internal order in Plato's Republic.
records.boundary_note: The tripartition is not a modern brain-module claim and should not be conflated with Freud's id, ego, and superego.

claim_scope.applies_to: Conflict among motivations and the structure of just agency.
claim_scope.does_not_establish: Neural localization or a uniform account across every Platonic dialogue.

evidence_profile.citation_mix: Republic digital edition plus SEP ancient-soul analysis.
evidence_profile.verification_summary: Project Gutenberg and SEP locators checked.

open_questions: Are the three parts literal subjects of attitudes or explanatory abstractions?
How does tripartition relate to the immortal soul in other dialogues?

records.name: Aristotelian faculty psychology in De Anima
records.status_note: The soul-as-form account is clear, while intellect in De Anima III.5 and its separability generated rival ancient and medieval interpretations.
records.summary: Aristotle defines soul as the first actuality of a natural organized body with life potentially and distinguishes nutritive, perceptual, desiderative, locomotive, imaginative, and intellectual powers. Faculties are analyzed by their characteristic objects and activities rather than as independent inner substances.
records.scope: Life-functions, perception, imagination, desire, and intellect in De Anima.
records.boundary_note: Aristotle's psychē means the principle of life and should not be imported wholesale as a Cartesian mind; the active-intellect passage needs separate interpretation.

claim_scope.applies_to: Powers characteristic of living organisms and their objects.
claim_scope.does_not_establish: A modern functionalist identity or a single uncontested doctrine of disembodied intellect.

evidence_profile.citation_mix: De Anima digital text plus SEP analysis.
evidence_profile.verification_summary: MIT Classics and SEP locators checked.

open_questions: How should active and receptive intellect be interpreted?
Are Aristotelian faculties best understood as capacities, forms, or explanatory levels?

records.name: Hobbesian materialist psychology
records.status_note: Hobbes is widely read as a materialist and mechanist, though exact relations among motion, representation, reasoning, and phenomenal appearance remain debated.
records.summary: Hobbes analyzes sensation as motion initiated by external bodies and continued through bodily organs, imagination as decaying sense, and reasoning as rule-governed reckoning. Human thought and appetite belong to nature rather than an incorporeal mental substance.
records.scope: Mechanistic accounts of sensation, imagination, appetite, and reasoning.
records.boundary_note: Hobbes's motions are embedded in seventeenth-century physics and should not be presented as an anticipatory neural identity theory without qualification.

claim_scope.applies_to: Naturalistic explanation of mental operations through bodily motion.
claim_scope.does_not_establish: The adequacy of contemporary reductive physicalism or a modern computational model.

evidence_profile.citation_mix: Leviathan digital edition plus SEP analysis.
evidence_profile.verification_summary: Project Gutenberg and SEP locators checked.

open_questions: How does Hobbes distinguish the causal motion from the appearing quality?
What explanatory role does language play in reasoning beyond sensory motion?

records.name: Malebranche's vision in God
records.status_note: Debate concerns whether ideas are divine archetypes, God's own ideas, or finite modes of presentation and how vision in God fits Malebranche's occasionalism.
records.summary: Malebranche argues that finite minds do not directly perceive material bodies through ideas produced by those bodies. They perceive intelligible ideas in God, while God alone is the true efficient cause of perceptual modifications in the mind.
records.scope: Objects of perception, divine ideas, and causal dependence of mind and body.
records.boundary_note: Vision in God is not the claim that perceivers become omniscient or directly inspect God's essence; finite perception remains limited and occasioned.

claim_scope.applies_to: How finite minds represent external bodies under occasionalism.
claim_scope.does_not_establish: A generic idealism or a contemporary empirical theory of vision.

evidence_profile.citation_mix: Cambridge companion chapter plus SEP overview.
evidence_profile.verification_summary: Cambridge DOI and SEP locator checked.

open_questions: What exactly are the ideas seen in God?
How are determinate perceptual modifications related to universal divine ideas?

records.name: Anne Conway's vital monism
records.status: historically significant recovered position · interpretation contested
records.status_note: Conway's created-substance monism, hierarchy of spirit and body, and theological commitments do not map neatly onto contemporary physicalism or panpsychism.
records.summary: Conway rejects both Cartesian dead matter and strict mind-body substance dualism. Created reality forms one living, transformable kind of substance in which spirit and body differ by degree, while God and Christ retain distinct metaphysical roles in her system.
records.scope: Continuity of created substance, life, perception, and mind-body transformation.
records.boundary_note: Calling the view monist refers to created substance and must not erase Conway's God–Christ–creation distinctions or her specific theological setting.

claim_scope.applies_to: Mind-body continuity and the living character of created beings.
claim_scope.does_not_establish: Contemporary panpsychism, materialism, or a secular process ontology.

evidence_profile.verification_summary: Cambridge DOI and SEP locator checked.

records.name: Margaret Cavendish's self-moving perceptive matter
aliases: Cavendish on perceptive and rational matter
records.status_note: Scholars debate whether Cavendish is best read as materialist, vitalist, panpsychist, or organicist and how figurative language maps onto her natural philosophy.
records.summary: Cavendish treats nature as wholly material but intrinsically self-moving, with rational and sensitive matter participating in perception and action throughout natural bodies. Perception is an active patterning or self-figuration rather than passive reception of immaterial species.
records.scope: Material self-motion, perception, reason, and organization in nature.
records.boundary_note: Cavendish's rational and sensitive matter should not be equated without argument to contemporary microphenomenal panpsychism or modern information processing.

claim_scope.applies_to: How perception and agency can belong to an entirely material nature.
claim_scope.does_not_establish: A modern neural theory or that every particle is a miniature human subject.

records.name: Freudian dynamic unconscious
records.status: historically transformative · scientific and clinical claims deeply contested
records.status_note: Unconscious processing is broadly accepted in psychology, but Freud's dynamic, drive-based, symbolic, and therapeutic claims require separate evidence and are not equivalent to contemporary cognitive unconscious processes.
records.summary: Freud's dynamic unconscious consists not merely of currently unattended contents but of mental processes kept from consciousness through repression while continuing to shape symptoms, dreams, slips, affects, and action. Conflict and defense organize access between unconscious and conscious systems.
records.scope: Repressed mental processes, conflict, defense, and indirect expression.
records.boundary_note: The dynamic unconscious must not be treated as synonymous with all nonconscious neural processing, implicit memory, or subliminal perception.

claim_scope.applies_to: Unconscious wishes, representations, conflicts, and their defended access to consciousness.
claim_scope.does_not_establish: The validity of every Freudian drive, developmental, symbolic, or therapeutic claim.

evidence_profile.verification_summary: UPenn PDF and IEP locator and authorship checked.

open_questions: Which dynamic claims can be operationalized independently of interpretive circularity?

records.name: Existential-feelings framework
records.tradition: Contemporary phenomenology and philosophy of psychiatry
records.status: influential contemporary framework · construct boundaries contested
records.status_note: The framework is widely discussed in phenomenological psychopathology, while critics dispute how existential feelings differ from moods, emotions, bodily feelings, and pre-reflective beliefs.
records.summary: Ratcliffe calls background senses of reality, belonging, familiarity, possibility, estrangement, or unreality existential feelings. They are bodily ways of finding oneself in a world that shape the field of salient possibilities and intentional experience rather than standing as discrete feelings directed at one object.
records.scope: Background affective structures of world-experience in everyday life and psychopathology.
records.boundary_note: Existential feelings are not synonymous with existentialist emotion, clinical mood symptoms, or propositional beliefs that the world exists; individual forms require phenomenological and cultural differentiation.

claim_scope.applies_to: How bodily feeling structures an implicit sense of reality, situatedness, and available possibility.
claim_scope.does_not_establish: A single neural mechanism, diagnostic biomarker, or culture-invariant taxonomy.

evidence_profile.verification_summary: Oxford and De Gruyter DOIs checked.

records.name: Heideggerian being-in-the-world and disclosedness
records.status_note: Being and Time is not a psychology text; mind-related applications require distinguishing Heidegger's ontological analysis from empirical cognitive claims.
records.summary: Heidegger rejects the picture of an inner subject first confronted with an external world. Dasein is already being-in-the-world: practically involved with equipment, others, possibilities, and significance, within a prior disclosed field that makes explicit perception and judgment possible.
records.scope: Situated intelligibility, practical involvement, and conditions for encountering entities.
records.boundary_note: Being-in-the-world is not spatial containment, generic embodiment, or a direct scientific hypothesis about the brain.

claim_scope.applies_to: The prior structure of situated intelligibility and practical engagement.
claim_scope.does_not_establish: A cognitive architecture, representational theory, or universal empirical law.

records.name: Schelerian affective intentionality and person
records.status_note: Scheler's hierarchy of values and account of person are debated, and his political writings require historically critical treatment separate from the phenomenology.
records.summary: Scheler treats feeling as an intentional disclosure of value rather than a merely private bodily state. Sympathy, fellow-feeling, love, resentment, and emotional identification have distinct structures through which persons and values become manifest.
records.scope: Intentional affect, value-disclosure, interpersonal feeling, and the person.
records.boundary_note: Scheler distinguishes sympathy, empathy, emotional contagion, and identification; using them as synonyms destroys the framework's central taxonomy.

claim_scope.applies_to: How feeling presents values and interpersonal relations.
claim_scope.does_not_establish: A universal value hierarchy or a contemporary affective-neuroscience mechanism.

evidence_profile.verification_summary: Routledge and SEP locators checked.

records.name: Du Boisian double consciousness
records.status_note: Scholars distinguish early psychological, later political, and broader sociological uses across Du Bois's corpus; the construct is not reducible to individual pathology.
records.summary: Du Bois describes a racialized split in self-apprehension produced by viewing oneself through a society structured by anti-Black contempt while also sustaining one's own perspective and aspirations. The resulting 'two-ness' names conflict and critical insight within American social life.
records.scope: Socially mediated self-consciousness under racial domination.
records.boundary_note: Double consciousness is historically situated in Du Bois's analysis of the color line; it is not a diagnostic label for dissociative identity disorder or generic ambivalence.

claim_scope.applies_to: Racialized self-relation and perspective under U.S. anti-Black social structures.
claim_scope.does_not_establish: A universal invariant of every Black person's experience or a clinical disorder.

evidence_profile.verification_summary: Project Gutenberg and SEP locators checked.

open_questions: How do Du Bois's uses shift across periods and genres?

records.name: Fanon's epidermal racial schema and embodied subjectivity
records.tradition: Black existential phenomenology and anticolonial thought
records.status_note: Translations vary among corporeal, bodily, historico-racial, and epidermal schemas; the account is historically situated in colonial anti-Blackness.
records.summary: Fanon describes how the lived bodily schema is disrupted under the racializing look and overwritten by historical stereotypes and an epidermal racial schema. Embodied action and self-perception become mediated by colonial social meanings imposed on Blackness.
records.scope: Racialized embodiment, social visibility, alienation, and agency.
records.boundary_note: This is not a biological theory of race or a claim that bodily subjectivity is naturally racial; it analyzes historically produced colonial perception and constraint.

claim_scope.applies_to: How anti-Black social structures reorganize lived bodily possibility and self-relation.
claim_scope.does_not_establish: A uniform experience across all racialized people or eras.

evidence_profile.verification_summary: Warwick and SEP locators checked.

records.name: Al-Fārābī's faculty psychology and active intellect
records.status_note: Al-Fārābī's works differ in genre and purpose; exact chronology, immortality implications, and the integration of psychology with political philosophy remain debated.
records.summary: Al-Fārābī distinguishes nutritive, sensitive, appetitive, imaginative, and rational faculties. Human potential intellect becomes actual through intelligibles supplied or illuminated by a separate active intellect, while perfected imagination helps explain prophetic representations within his cosmological-political system.
records.era: 9th–10th centuries; later Arabic, Hebrew, and Latin reception

records.name: Ibn al-Haytham's intromission and inferential visual perception
records.tradition: Medieval Arabic optics and natural philosophy
records.status: historically foundational · interpretation of inference debated
records.status_note: His optical and perceptual analyses were transformative, but labels such as 'unconscious inference' are retrospective and must be tied to exact passages.
records.summary: Ibn al-Haytham argues that light and color from visible objects enter the eye rather than visual rays issuing from it. Vision combines optical reception with discriminations and judgments shaped by prior experience, including rapid processes whose temporal interval may go unnoticed.
records.scope: Optical input, ocular conditions, visual discrimination, and perceptual judgment.
records.boundary_note: The theory is not a modern retinal-neural model, and 'unconscious inference' is an interpretive bridge rather than Ibn al-Haytham's own technical term.

records.name: Ibn ʿArabī's imaginal perception and barzakh
records.status: historically influential · terminology and corpus interpretation contested
records.status_note: Ibn ʿArabī's large Arabic corpus and later Akbarian reception require work-level attribution; 'imaginal' is a scholarly translation with a specific history.
records.summary: Ibn ʿArabī gives imagination a mediating or barzakh function: it joins and distinguishes sensory and intelligible domains and makes forms present without reducing them to either ordinary bodies or abstractions. Dream, vision, and symbolic form require disciplined interpretation within his metaphysical and spiritual framework.
records.scope: Imagination as an intermediate mode of manifestation and perception in Ibn ʿArabī's works.
records.boundary_note: The imaginal is not mere fantasy, and this named Akbarian account must not be presented as a universal Islamic doctrine or empirical paranormal evidence.

claim_scope.applies_to: Mediation among sensible, intelligible, symbolic, and revelatory forms in Ibn ʿArabī.

records.name: Gersonides' acquired intellect and active intellect
aliases: Levi ben Gerson's psychology of intellect
records.status_note: Gersonides' technical arguments concern acquired knowledge, individuation, and active intellect; personal survival and conjunction require careful textual qualification.
records.summary: Gersonides distinguishes material or potential intellect, acquired intellect formed through actual knowledge, and a separate active intellect that embodies the intelligible order of the sublunary world. Human intellectual achievement constitutes what may persist, rather than an unqualified continuation of every psychological feature.
records.scope: Acquisition of intelligibles, active intellect, individuation, and intellectual persistence.
records.boundary_note: The account is not identical with Averroes' unity thesis or Maimonides' position, and 'immortality' must not imply retention of ordinary autobiographical consciousness without argument.

claim_scope.does_not_establish: Personal immortality in an ordinary psychological sense or a common medieval Jewish consensus.

records.name: Buber's I–Thou relational selfhood
records.tradition: Modern Jewish philosophy and dialogical thought
records.status: historically influential · theological and ethical interpretations vary
records.status_note: I–Thou and I–It name relational orientations, not fixed types of object; Buber's Hasidic, biblical, existential, and dialogical contexts should remain visible.
records.summary: Buber distinguishes the I–Thou relation, in which another is addressed as a whole presence, from I–It engagement, in which entities are experienced and used as objects. records.scope: Dialogical relation, personhood, encounter, and objectification.
records.boundary_note: I–It is not simply immoral and I–Thou is not a permanent emotional state; practical object-relation is unavoidable, while dialogical relation has a distinct mode.

claim_scope.applies_to: How modes of address and encounter constitute forms of selfhood.
claim_scope.does_not_establish: A cognitive theory of mindreading or a uniform Jewish doctrine.

evidence_profile.verification_summary: Publisher and SEP locators checked.

records.name: Madhva's Dvaita plural selves and dependent consciousness
records.status: living scholastic-religious tradition · internally developed reception
records.status_note: Madhva's writings and later Mādhva commentators require distinction; interpretations of hierarchy, grace, agency, and soul-destiny are especially contested.
records.summary: Madhva argues that individual selves are eternally real and mutually distinct, remain distinct from Viṣṇu/Brahman, and depend on the independent divine reality. Liberation does not erase numerical individuality or collapse a self into an undifferentiated consciousness.
records.scope: Ontological difference among God, individual selves, and world in Madhva's Vedānta.
records.boundary_note: Dvaita here means Madhva's named Vedāntic realism, not generic mind-body dualism; later doctrinal developments and contested soul hierarchies must not be attributed indiscriminately to every practitioner.

claim_scope.does_not_establish: A uniform Hindu theory of consciousness or Cartesian substance dualism.

records.name: Dignāga–Dharmakīrti apoha theory of conceptual content
records.status: historically foundational · versions and translations contested
records.status_note: Dignāga's and Dharmakīrti's formulations are not identical, and later Tibetan and Sanskrit commentators develop multiple exclusion accounts.
records.summary: Apoha theories explain conceptual and linguistic content through exclusion—roughly, a term such as 'cow' functions by excluding what is non-cow rather than by apprehending a real universal shared by all cows. Dharmakīrti embeds exclusion within causal, inferential, and pragmatic accounts of cognition.
records.era: 5th–7th centuries; later Indian and Tibetan reception
records.scope: How concepts and words classify particulars without real universals.
records.boundary_note: Apoha is distinct from the corpus's existing reflexive-awareness record; it addresses conceptual content and semantics, and it is not one unchanged doctrine across authors.

claim_scope.applies_to: Concept formation, linguistic reference, and classification of particulars.
claim_scope.does_not_establish: That all Buddhist schools deny meaning or share a nominalist theory.

evidence_profile.citation_mix: Routledge apoha analysis plus SEP Dharmakīrti context.
evidence_profile.verification_summary: Routledge DOI and SEP locator checked.

records.name: Mencian heart-mind and four sprouts
records.status: historically foundational · interpretive and translation debates
records.status_note: The relation among innate tendencies, cultivated virtue, affect, reflection, and social conditions differs across passages and later commentaries.
records.summary: The Mengzi describes affective-cognitive 'sprouts' or beginnings—compassion, shame and dislike, deference, and approval and disapproval—that can develop into benevolence, righteousness, ritual propriety, and wisdom. The heart-mind (xīn) both feels and reflects, and cultivation is required for the sprouts to grow.
records.scope: Affective-cognitive tendencies, moral agency, reflection, and cultivation.
records.boundary_note: Xīn is not cleanly equivalent to either English 'mind' or 'heart,' and the sprouts are incipient tendencies rather than fully formed virtues or brain modules.

claim_scope.applies_to: Mencian accounts of affect, judgment, motivation, and cultivated character.
claim_scope.does_not_establish: A uniform Chinese theory of mind or innate moral perfection without cultivation.

evidence_profile.citation_mix: Chinese Text Project passage locator plus SEP analysis.
evidence_profile.verification_summary: Primary passage and SEP locator checked.

open_questions: How should xīn, qí, and qíng be translated across passages?
How do spontaneous affect and reflective endorsement interact in cultivation?

records.name: Zhu Xi's heart-mind, nature, and feelings
aliases: Zhu Xi on xin xing qing
Neo-Confucian heart-mind cultivation in Zhu Xi
records.status_note: Zhu Xi's vocabulary and synthesis developed across genres; later orthodoxy and East Asian receptions must not be collapsed into his own position.
records.summary: Zhu Xi analyzes the heart-mind as the master of the person, coordinating nature (xìng), feelings (qíng), intention, and awareness through the interaction of pattern (lǐ) and psychophysical stuff (qì). Cultivation joins investigation of things, attentiveness, and regulation of affect rather than suppressing feeling wholesale.
records.scope: Heart-mind, moral psychology, pattern, psychophysical endowment, and cultivation.
records.boundary_note: Lǐ and qì are not simply mental form and physical matter, and Zhu Xi's view is distinct from Wang Yangming's later school of heart-mind already represented in the corpus.

claim_scope.applies_to: Zhu Xi's relation among nature, feeling, cognition, and disciplined cultivation.
claim_scope.does_not_establish: A uniform East Asian account or modern substance dualism.

evidence_profile.citation_mix: Oxford selected writings plus SEP analysis.
evidence_profile.verification_summary: OUP DOI and SEP locator checked.

open_questions: How should changing formulations across letters, dialogues, and commentaries be versioned?
What is the exact role of attentiveness (jìng) in cognition and affect regulation?

records.name: Fazang's Huayan interpenetration and One Mind
records.status_note: Fazang's systematic classifications, metaphors, and relation to the Awakening of Faith differ from later Huayan thinkers such as Chengguan and Zongmi.
records.summary: Fazang uses doctrines of dependent arising, the six characteristics, and mutual inclusion to articulate how distinct phenomena can be nonobstructively interdependent without losing conventional distinction. His One Mind language participates in a Buddhist soteriological and textual framework rather than positing one numerically singular cosmic subject.
records.scope: Mutual inclusion, interpenetration, One Mind discourse, and Huayan contemplative-metaphysical analysis.
records.boundary_note: Interpenetration is not evidence that all entities share one phenomenal subject, and 'One Mind' must not be flattened into Western absolute idealism or generic cosmic consciousness.

claim_scope.applies_to: Fazang's accounts of relational structure and mind within Huayan soteriology.
claim_scope.does_not_establish: A universal East Asian view, a modern field theory, or a single experiencer underlying all beings.

evidence_profile.citation_mix: SEP Huayan analysis plus DOI-indexed study of Fazang's six characteristics.
evidence_profile.verification_summary: SEP locator and Taylor & Francis DOI checked.

open_questions: How should Fazang's One Mind language be distinguished from Zongmi's later synthesis?
Which metaphors describe logical, ontological, contemplative, or pedagogical relations?

records.name: Kūkai's ten stages of mind
records.status: historically foundational · text and classification interpretation contested
records.status_note: Kūkai's Ten Abodes of Mind and Precious Key organize stages differently in detail; later Shingon exegesis must be distinguished from his own texts.
records.summary: Kūkai organizes modes of mind and religious understanding into ten stages culminating in esoteric realization associated with Mahāvairocana. The scheme is simultaneously doctrinal classification, soteriological path, and account of transformed cognition, not a developmental scale validated by modern psychology.
records.scope: Doctrinal and soteriological classifications of mind in Kūkai's esoteric Buddhism.
records.boundary_note: The stages are not IQ levels, neural states, or a neutral ranking of world religions; they arise in Kūkai's polemical and ritual-soteriological context.

claim_scope.applies_to: Kūkai's ordering of modes of understanding and esoteric realization.
claim_scope.does_not_establish: An empirical hierarchy of consciousness or consensus across Japanese Buddhism.

evidence_profile.citation_mix: SEP Kūkai overview plus J-STAGE analysis of self-nature and the ten-stage system.
evidence_profile.verification_summary: SEP locator and J-STAGE DOI checked.

open_questions: How do the two principal ten-stage texts qualify one another?
What roles do ritual, mantra, visualization, and doctrinal classification play in transformation of mind?

records.name: Menkiti–Gyekye communitarian personhood debate
aliases: Menkiti-Gyekye debate on person and community
records.status: major scholarly debate · labels and interpretations contested
records.status_note: The familiar 'radical Menkiti/moderate Gyekye' contrast is itself challenged; later philosophers dispute whether it accurately captures either position.
records.summary: Menkiti emphasizes personhood as normatively achieved through communal incorporation and moral maturation, while Gyekye argues for a moderate communitarianism that preserves individual capacities, rights, and some independent worth. The dispute concerns moral personhood, social constitution, and the priority of community rather than a simple collective-versus-individual binary.
proponents: Motsamai Molefe as a critical reinterpreter
records.scope: Normative personhood, communal formation, rights, autonomy, and moral achievement.
records.boundary_note: This is a debate among named philosophers, not 'the African view of personhood.' The radical/moderate labels are retrospective and actively disputed.

claim_scope.applies_to: How communal relations and moral development bear on personhood and individual standing.
claim_scope.does_not_establish: A pan-African consensus or denial of baseline moral status to children and disabled people.

evidence_profile.citation_mix: SEP context plus Molefe's direct reassessment of the debate.
evidence_profile.verification_summary: SEP locator and Berghahn DOI checked.

open_questions: Does Menkiti defend ontological priority, normative achievement, or both?
Can communal formation coexist with inalienable baseline personhood and rights?

records.name: Te Whare Tapa Whā model of Māori wellbeing
records.domain: Wellbeing, mental life, spirit, body & whānau
records.tradition: Māori health scholarship in Aotearoa New Zealand
records.status: widely used living health framework · locally contextual
records.status_note: The model is used in health, education, and community practice; implementation should remain accountable to Māori authority, local iwi and hapū context, and later refinements.
records.summary: Mason Durie's whare model presents hauora as supported by interconnected taha tinana (physical), taha hinengaro (mental and emotional), taha wairua (spiritual), and taha whānau (family and social) dimensions, grounded in whenua. Weakness in one wall affects the integrity of the whole.
proponents: Māori health practitioners and communities in situated applications
records.scope: Holistic Māori health and wellbeing across bodily, mental-emotional, spiritual, relational, and land-grounded dimensions.
records.boundary_note: This is a health and wellbeing model, not a stand-alone theory of phenomenal consciousness. Māori terms should remain primary, and the model must not be generalized to all Indigenous peoples.

claim_scope.applies_to: Holistic assessment and support of hauora in Māori contexts.
claim_scope.does_not_establish: A universal Indigenous psychology, a metaphysics of mind, or one fixed interpretation across iwi and hapū.

evidence_profile.citation_mix: Durie's original article plus government-maintained model description.
evidence_profile.verification_summary: Elsevier DOI and Ministry of Health locator checked.

open_questions: How do iwi-, hapū-, age-, and service-specific applications adapt the model?
How should whenua and colonization be represented when simplified diagrams omit them?

records.name: Hallowell's ethnographic account of Northern Ojibwe other-than-human persons
records.tradition: Historical anthropology of Northern Ojibwe communities at Berens River
records.status: influential ethnographic account · historical and methodological limits require explicit review
records.status_note: The record reports Hallowell's mid-twentieth-century interpretation based on fieldwork and named collaborators; contemporary Ojibwe and Anishinaabe scholarship must not be replaced by it.
records.summary: Hallowell reported that among Northern Ojibwe interlocutors at Berens River, the category of person could include some nonhuman beings and objects as contextually agentive, communicative, and socially related. His phrase 'other-than-human persons' describes an ethnographic person-category broader than biological humanity.
proponents: William Berens and other Northern Ojibwe interlocutors as indispensable but historically undercredited knowledge holders
records.scope: A historically situated ethnographic account of person categories and social relations at Berens River.
records.boundary_note: This is Hallowell's external ethnographic account, not a timeless or universal 'Ojibwe ontology.' It should not be relabeled generic animism, generalized across Anishinaabe nations, or treated as community authorization to disclose restricted knowledge.

claim_scope.applies_to: Hallowell's published interpretation of specified Northern Ojibwe conversations and practices.
claim_scope.does_not_establish: Uniform belief among all Ojibwe or Indigenous peoples, or scientific evidence that every object is conscious.

basis: critical scholarly edited collection and fieldwork context
evidence_profile.citation_mix: Columbia chapter DOI plus Nebraska Press contextualized collection.
evidence_profile.verification_summary: Publisher DOI and university-press locator checked.

open_questions: How do contemporary community scholars assess Hallowell's categories, translations, and attribution practices?
Which claims should be corrected, supplemented, or withheld under community protocols?
